# NSPanel HAUI 0.4.5

This release adds a live preview of the panel to the editor, draws every panel
card from the hub's own render, moves firmware updates into the integration
(with installs from a URL or a local file and a master switch per panel) and
brings Day/Night profiles, editable popups, cycle cards on the weather panel, a
light background and a long list of display and notification fixes. It
requires Home Assistant 2026.11.

## Before updating

The [upgrade guide](docs/update.md) covers the update order and the automatic
page-switching migration. [Update Process](docs/update-process.md#upgrading)
has the step-by-step details for every breaking change.

- **Home Assistant 2026.11 required; HACS replaced by the Marketplace** —
  `hacs.json` declares `2026.11`, the release whose built-in Marketplace
  replaces HACS, and the install docs describe only the Marketplace (**Settings
  → Marketplace → Add from link**, `happydasch/nspanel_haui`; adding a custom
  repository needs a GitHub connection). Home Assistant migrates HACS installs
  on the first start of 2026.11 and they keep receiving updates; dev builds
  follow the repository's **Pre-release** switch. The development pin moves to
  `homeassistant==2026.11.0`, and the unused HACS `info.md` is gone. See
  [Upgrading → Home Assistant 2026.11](docs/update-process.md#15-home-assistant-202611-and-the-marketplace).
- **Firmware updates moved from the firmware to the integration** — the
  firmware drops its `update: platform: http_request` **HAUI Firmware** entity
  and the `firmware_manifest_url` substitution; ESPHome keeps only its stock
  dashboard update entity. The integration now provides the **HAUI Firmware**
  entity, reads the release manifest itself and installs through the
  firmware's `install_firmware_url` action, so panels on firmware 0.4.2 (which
  lacks that action) must be updated once by hand. A test panel that followed
  local test releases through the substitution needs the new **Firmware
  manifest URL** device setting instead. See
  [Upgrading → Firmware updates](docs/update-process.md#11-firmware-updates-moved-to-the-integration).
- **Firmware build variants fail closed** — a custom build from
  `esphome/install.yaml` (or the dev config) reports its variant and is never
  offered or installed the public universal release image, whose baked
  credentials would silently replace the panel's own. Panels whose firmware
  does not report a variant (0.4.3 and earlier) are treated the same: flash
  the new release once by hand (ESPHome or **Install firmware → From URL**),
  then the hub can update them again. The release manifest carries
  `"variant": "universal"`, the device state `firmware_variant`.
- **The display TFT follows the firmware manifest (one update path)** — the
  manifest each release ships now carries a `tft` block (version + per display
  model asset); the **HAUI Display** entity and the TFT install actions read
  it instead of looking up a matching GitHub release. The editor's TFT picker
  therefore lists only the manifest's TFT (plus **From URL**); installing an
  older release's TFT by version is no longer possible — use **From URL** for
  that. A manifest without a `tft` block (a local test release names none)
  offers no display update at all instead of failing to find a release. See
  [Upgrading → Display TFT updates](docs/update-process.md#12-display-tft-updates-come-from-the-firmware-manifest).
- **Native OTA is encrypted with the API key** — the `ota: platform: esphome`
  block uses `encryption:` (inheriting `api_encryption_key`) instead of
  `password: $ota_password`, so builds no longer warn that the password wastes
  flash and RAM; the `ota_password` substitution and secret are gone. The
  `on_begin` suspend hook and the `http_request` OTA platform are unchanged.
  Panels on 0.4 firmware need no migration install: their ESPHome 2026.10 build
  already compiles the OTA Noise key from `api: encryption`, so the first
  encrypted upload succeeds as-is. Only firmware built with an older ESPHome
  (0.3.x and earlier) needs one install with `allow_plaintext_upload`, and a
  `password:` on the OTA block of your own YAML now fails validation
  ([#81](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/issues/81)). See
  [ESPHome → Encrypted native OTA](docs/esphome.md#encrypted-native-ota).
- **The Current Page sensor moved to the firmware** — the firmware's
  **Current Page** text sensor replaces the integration's sensor platform. Its
  value is still the Nextion page name. Delete the old, now unavailable
  `sensor.<device>_current_page` entity so the firmware's entity can take that
  ID (otherwise it becomes `..._2`). The `panel`, `type` and `title` attributes
  are gone; use the `nspanel_haui.page_changed` event for those. The
  firmware's sensor is disabled by default: enable it on the panel's ESPHome
  device page. See
  [Upgrading → Current Page sensor](docs/update-process.md#14-the-current-page-sensor-moved-to-the-firmware).
- **Unused firmware actions and events removed** — the firmware drops the
  `haui_discover`, `req_device_info` and `req_reconnect` actions and the
  `use_relay_left`/`use_relay_right` events. The hub never called or listened
  to them (it finds panels through the ESPHome device registry and reads the
  versions from the device state), so panels work as before; an automation
  that used one switches to `req_device_state`, `hub_connection_closed` or a
  state trigger on the **Use Relay** switches. See
  [Upgrading → Unused firmware actions](docs/update-process.md#16-unused-firmware-actions-and-events-removed).
- **Services fail on a device that is no panel** — the `nspanel_haui` services
  raise an error when their `device` matches no running panel. They logged a
  warning and did nothing before, so the call looked successful. An automation
  whose `device` names a disabled or removed panel, or another integration's
  device, now stops at that step: pick the panel's **NSPanel HAUI** device (the
  one the device selector offers) or its ESPHome device, or set
  `continue_on_error: true` on a step that may target a disabled panel. See
  [Upgrading → Services](docs/update-process.md#18-services-fail-on-a-device-that-is-no-panel).
- **Automatic page switching moved from the firmware to the hub** — the
  firmware drops the **Use Auto-Page** switch, the **Timeout Page** number and
  the `esphome.timeout` page-timeout event; the integration drops the
  `hub_idle_timeout` device setting. The hub owns the once-a-second idle-page
  check and each page's hold, while `use_auto_page`/`timeout_page` stay device
  settings. An empty Night idle key no longer inherits the Day destination.
  Delete the two orphaned ESPHome entities and remove automations that used the
  old event. Update the integration first, then install the matching firmware
  with **HAUI Firmware** and let its matching TFT follow; mixed hub and firmware
  versions are unsupported. See [the upgrade guide](docs/update.md#automatic-page-switching-moved-to-the-hub).

## New

- **Live preview in the editor** — the new **Live preview** button
  (`mdi:television-play`) opens an interactive virtual panel for the selected
  device, rendered from the real hub code: tap, drag and swipe with mouse or
  finger, press the hardware buttons, trigger the idle timeout. **Sandbox
  mode** (the default) simulates every entity change; **Live mode** calls Home
  Assistant, including the panel's relays from the hardware buttons, except
  for the panel's settings; switching Live mode on drops the simulated states.
  A **Simulated/Live** switch and a mode note above the screen say which mode
  is active and what it does. **More tools** shows the **Show entities** switch
  (hidden by default) and **Reset sandbox** (Simulated mode only, disabled until
  a simulated state changed), which drops the simulated states so the preview
  shows the real Home Assistant states again; hiding the tools again switches
  entity hover off, and the **Idle timeout** button sits in the bar. The screen
  and the two hardware buttons sit in one frame, and each button carries a light
  that shows its relay in blue, or the state of the entity it switches in
  yellow (on/off for switches, open/closed by position for covers, and the
  active state for locks, climate, alarm, media and timer entities). **Show
  entities** names the entity under the mouse, including the weather info
  cards and the vacuum battery button. **Notifications are mirrored
  read-only** in either mode: the preview polls the panel's current queue and
  applies it to its own notification controller, so a notification queued on
  the panel (or one that opens with force-show) appears in the preview, and
  dismissing it in the preview leaves the panel's queue unchanged. The preview
  fires no events for automations and never installs
  updates. A device has one virtual Simulated copy, shared by its open
  Simulated previews and its panel cards; it follows every save. Live previews
  are independent of it and of each other.
  Contributed by [@jameshiscott](https://github.com/jameshiscott) in
  [#85](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/pull/85) and
  [#86](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/pull/86).
- **Panel cards drawn by the hub** — every panel card (user panels, system
  panels, popup aliases, landscape and portrait) shows its panel exactly as the
  device does: the hub renders the panel and the card replays the hub's
  display output in the Nextion simulator, built from the real HMI layout.
  Entity values, translations in the device's language, templates, the clock,
  the weather forecast and colour overrides are the hub's own; unsaved edits
  show right away, and a popup's card opens it for a sample (an entity of its
  domain, one that is on if there is one, an example notification or
  selection). The dozens of per-type preview renderers and the browser-side
  copy of the hub's rendering are gone: a new panel type needs only a correct
  `PageDescriptor.page_id`.
- **Screens overview** — the
  [Screens overview](https://happydasch.github.io/nspanel_haui/screens.html)
  shows every panel, popup and system screen in the landscape and portrait
  layout, rendered by the hub itself with sample data. The new **Screens**
  workflow regenerates the page and its PNGs (`docs/assets/screens/`) after
  each dev firmware build and commits them when a screen changed
  (`gen_preview_gallery.py --docs`). The README, the panel overview and the
  panel pages show these screenshots instead of the hand-drawn previews.
- **Every popup can be edited** — the editor's System Panels section offers
  **Edit** on every popup (`popup_*`), no longer only six entity popups
  (`popup_alarm`, `popup_timer`, Notify, Select and Unlock were missing). An
  edited popup keeps the built-in defaults it does not set, keeps its key and
  never joins navigation. On the popups the hub drives (Notify, Select,
  Unlock) the editor hides **Panel pin** and **Close automatically after** and
  the hub ignores them: a PIN on Unlock would re-open Unlock forever. System,
  Blank, Settings and About stay fixed: their cards are read-only, the API
  refuses a panel saved under their key, and the store drops one an earlier
  dev build saved (logged as a warning).
- **HAUI Firmware update entity in the integration** — each linked panel gets
  `update.<device>_haui_firmware` next to **HAUI Display**: installed version
  `yaml_version`, latest version from the firmware manifest, *installing* (and
  available) while the panel flashes and reboots. The hub fires
  `nspanel_haui.firmware_update_changed` events for it. An install that does
  not end in a reboot within ten minutes, or a reboot into the old version, is
  reported as an error instead of staying *installing*. The entity id the
  firmware's own entity held is reclaimed once ESPHome removed that entity.
  - **Firmware update channel** — `update.firmware_update_channel` (`stable` or
    `dev`, default `stable`) picks the manifest the entity follows: the latest
    stable GitHub release, or the newest release in the GitHub release list,
    dev prereleases included. The panel's release notice follows the channel
    too: `stable` ignores prereleases.
  - **Firmware manifest URL** — `update.firmware_manifest_url` (device editor →
    Updates) names the manifest explicitly and overrides the channel; empty
    means the channel's manifest. Test panels point it at the manifest
    `scripts/dev_release.py` writes.
- **Install update from the editor** — **Install update** in a panel's
  **Info** dialog installs the display TFT or the firmware. The display choice
  offers the TFT the firmware needs, the firmware choice the offered update or
  another release that ships an OTA image; both take **From URL** and
  **From local file**. A local file is a compiled Nextion `.tft` (up to
  16 MiB) or an ESPHome OTA app image (`.bin`,
  not a factory image): the hub checks its Nextion signature or ESP image
  header and the app-partition size, keeps it in memory for up to an hour and
  hands the panel a random download URL on Home Assistant's **Internal URL**.
  See [Updating → Installing a local TFT or firmware image](docs/update.md#installing-a-local-tft-or-firmware-image).
- **Updates can be switched off per panel** — **Enable updates** in the
  device editor's **Updates** section is a master switch: when it is off the
  hub checks nothing and installs nothing, the panel's HAUI Firmware and HAUI
  Display entities become unavailable and the editor's install actions are
  refused. An update already in progress finishes. **Enable periodic update
  checks** turns the hourly check off and on without clearing the interval.
- **Color schemes replace the per-device palette** — **Device Colors** now
  manages a scheme library instead of editing one device's palette. Built-in
  schemes are **Dark Color** (the default), **Light Color** (white page, light
  grey header and controls, dark text), **White** (white page and header, dark
  text) and **Black** (black page and header, near-black controls). Each scheme
  defines the page roles (background, header, text, controls and entity states)
  and both the dark- and light-background weather, alarm and climate icon
  colors, so state icons stay readable on either background. A device stores
  the scheme ID (`color_scheme_id`) rather than a copy of the palette; the
  separate **Default icon color variant** setting (`color_scheme`, `dark` or
  `light`) picks the icon palette entity pages use, and a page with a static
  background uses that background's variant. See
  [Device Configuration → Color schemes](docs/configuration/device.md#color-schemes).
- **Custom schemes and JSON libraries** — built-in schemes are read-only.
  **Save as** creates a custom scheme, which can be renamed or deleted and is
  shared by every device in the hub; editing it updates every device that
  selects it. **Export** writes the custom library as versioned JSON
  (`version: 1`) and **Import** adds schemes, refusing duplicate IDs or names
  (including a name that duplicates a built-in); a scheme still selected by a
  device cannot be deleted. A device YAML export includes the selected custom
  scheme's definition, and importing the YAML restores it; importing a
  conflicting definition is refused. See
  [Device Configuration → Color schemes](docs/configuration/device.md#color-schemes).
- **Legacy colour overrides and migration** — on solid-colour pages and pages
  set to **Use color scheme**, an existing device keeps its saved
  `color_overrides` and old panel/item colour values, and they take precedence
  over the selected scheme. **Reset existing device and panel color
  overrides** in the Colors dialog clears them when applying a scheme; this
  removes the old Grid tile, Alarm keypad/action-button and Clock Two word
  colours. The generic per-item `color` option stays for deliberate
  entity-specific styling. A device from an older version whose saved
  background override is pure white migrates to the **Light Color** scheme;
  every other device starts on **Dark Color**.
- **Use color scheme backgrounds** — Clock, Clock Two and Weather gain a
  **Use color scheme** background. Instead of a decorative image it uses the
  TFT's solid dark or light fill chosen from the active scheme's `background`
  colour by its brightness, and the scheme's text, cycle-card and icon
  colours. Every decorative image now has an explicit light/dark contrast
  mapping (currently **Light Color** is light; the other images are dark),
  which controls text, time/date cards and domain icons together. **Light
  Color** remains an off-white image background, and **Dark** is now called
  **Dark Color** (saved panels keep their background). These colours and the
  solid fills need the display TFT that ships with 0.4.5: until **HAUI
  Display** installs it, solid pages keep their compiled colors and picture
  backgrounds can show the wrong picture. See
  [Device Configuration → Background pages](docs/configuration/device.md#background-pages).
- **Current Page Number sensor** — the firmware's new **Current Page Number**
  sensor reports the Nextion page id (`9` for `grid`) next to **Current
  Page**'s name. Both are disabled by default; enable them on the panel's
  ESPHome device page (see [ESPHome → Page](docs/esphome.md#page)).
- **Day/Night profiles** — each device can select Day and Night display
  settings by a fixed local window or Home Assistant sunrise/sunset with minute
  offsets. Profiles cover brightness, dimming, page/idle target and display-off
  behavior; the independent Sleep schedule keeps its existing precedence.
  Existing brightness/ramp values are adopted on first activation, and when
  scheduling is disabled those ESPHome values remain manual. See
  [Device Configuration](docs/configuration/device.md#daynight-profiles).
- **Cycle cards on the weather panel, entity cards and card timing** — the
  clock's cycle cards (time, date, outside and inside temperature in the big
  time area) now run on the weather panel too, with the same options in a new
  **Cycle cards** editor section on both panels. **Card entities** add up to
  four entities as extra cards (value large, name below), and **Seconds per
  card** / **First card pause** replace the fixed 5 s / 15 s. The card on
  screen redraws when its value changes (weather temperature, inside sensor,
  card entity). A card too wide for the time area is drawn in a smaller font
  rather than cut, so the date card always keeps its weekday ("Mon 16"). The
  weather panel's time area takes no touch, so its cards only cycle; tapping
  to skip ahead stays a clock feature.
- **Inside temperature sensor picker** — clock and weather panels can use any
  `sensor` entity for the inside temperature; leave it empty for the NSPanel's
  internal sensor.
- **Long press to go back** — Clock, ClockTwo and Weather panels have no
  header buttons and could only be left by swiping. The new **Long press to go
  back** panel option (Advanced section) goes back on a one-second hold
  anywhere: to the panel this one was opened from, or to the home panel. Also
  contributed by [@jameshiscott](https://github.com/jameshiscott).
- **Alarm panel action-button options** — an **Action buttons** section in the
  alarm panel editor: **Hidden arm modes** leaves supported modes off the
  buttons (e.g. no *Home*), and **Show action icons** puts the target state's
  icon before each label (left out when icon and label exceed the 10-byte
  button text). The button colours follow the active color scheme (the alarm
  state palette for the active dark/light variant). Contributed by
  [@quentinjourdan](https://github.com/quentinjourdan) in
  [#75](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/pull/75).

## Changed

- **Portrait function buttons are back in the header** — the four function
  buttons left the bottom bar (y 430..480) and sit at the ends of the header,
  as in landscape. The pages now use the full height: bottom controls, entity
  shortcuts, forecasts, media sources and the system messages moved down into
  the freed space. The change ships in the portrait TFT.
- **Row toggles are a switch icon** — the row panel's toggle was a filled box.
  It is now an icon on the page `background`: `mdi:toggle-switch-outline` in
  `component_active` when on, `mdi:toggle-switch-off-outline` in
  `text_inactive` when off.
- **Per-panel colour options follow the color scheme** — the Grid tile colours
  (`text_color`, `back_color`, `color_pressed`, `back_color_pressed`,
  `power_color`), the Alarm keypad and action-button colours, and Clock Two's
  `off_color`, `letter_color` and `special_color` default to the visible scheme.
  They stay optional overrides: set one to pin that colour, leave it empty to
  follow the scheme. Values saved by an older version are ordinary overrides
  now and can be cleared with **Reset existing device and panel color
  overrides** in **Device Colors**; the generic item `color` remains for
  deliberate entity-specific styling. **Show Power Button** remains a grid item
  option.
- **Single-entity panels handle missing or unavailable entities** — Light,
  Media, Vacuum, Cover, Climate and Alarm accept an empty item and hide their
  entity-specific content until one is configured. A configured entity that is
  unavailable or `unknown` hides its controls (playback, volume, power,
  keypad, sliders, action buttons) instead of leaving a stale or blank screen;
  Light, Media and Vacuum also show **Unavailable**, while the vacuum battery
  sensor and secondary items stay independent. An `unknown` state now counts
  as unavailable everywhere, so tapping such a tile opens the Unavailable
  message instead of running its action. The Light panel also falls back to
  the panel title when the entity has no name.
- **Cycle cards are off by default** — clock and weather panels show only the
  time until more cards are enabled in the **Cycle cards** section. Clock
  panels cycled the date and outside temperature by default before: turn on
  **Show date** and **Show outside temperature** to keep that (see
  [Upgrading → Cycle cards](docs/update-process.md#17-cycle-cards-are-off-by-default)).
  A clock panel without a weather entity skips the outside temperature card
  instead of showing `--°C`.
- **Screen Power is disabled by default** — like **Restart Display**; entities
  already enabled stay enabled.
- **Firmware versions compare like Home Assistant** — the hub compares versions
  with the same `AwesomeVersion` semantics the HAUI Firmware/HAUI Display
  entities use, so the two never disagree: a final release is offered over its
  dev builds (`0.4.5` over `0.4.5.dev3`), and an unparseable installed version
  (for example an old `dev-<run>-<sha>` build) is withheld as unknown instead
  of being re-offered on every check. Home Assistant falls back to "update
  available" when it cannot compare an offered version, so an unparseable
  manifest `version` is withheld from the HAUI Firmware entity the same way.
  Dev builds are validated to report a parseable next-patch version
  (`X.Y.(Z+1).dev<run>`).
- **Dev prereleases ship the display TFTs** — each `dev` prerelease attaches
  `nspanel_haui.tft` and `nspanel_haui_portrait.tft` and names them in its
  manifest's `tft` block, like a stable release. The TFT version is the
  `system.tftVersion` of the committed HMIs, and the dev firmware requires
  exactly that TFT, so a panel on the `dev` channel installs the matching TFT
  after a firmware update instead of keeping the last stable one.
- **A screen change must bump the display TFT version** — the push/PR checks
  compare both Nextion HMIs and `tft_version` in
  `esphome/nspanel_haui/version.yaml` against the PR's merge base (or the
  commit a push came from) and fail when an HMI changed under an unchanged or
  older TFT version. A panel only installs a display image newer than the one
  it reports, so a screen change committed under the old version would never
  reach it. The check (`scripts/verify_nextion/check_hmi_bump.py`) runs with
  the other Nextion gates on every push and PR; its failure names the bump
  command and reminds you to recompile both TFTs. See
  [Release](docs/release.md#published-development-firmware).
- **Firmware installs wait for you by default** — **Auto-install firmware
  updates** (`update.firmware_auto_update`) is now off by default (it was on),
  because an automatic install could flash a new firmware before the
  integration was updated or the release notes were read. Panels that never
  changed the setting now offer new firmware on their **HAUI Firmware** entity
  and wait for **Install**; turn the setting on in the device editor's
  **Updates** section to keep unattended installs. The display TFT still
  follows a firmware update on its own (**Auto-install TFT updates** stays on).
- **Device Manager and Device Info** — the Device Manager finds new HAUI panels
  among Home Assistant's ESPHome devices each time it opens and offers them for
  adding, so the **Scan** button is gone. It no longer hosts installs: the
  per-device install picker is gone, and the actions live in the panel's
  **Info** dialog — **Install update** (display TFT or firmware, including
  releases, URL and local file), **Redraw display** and **Download firmware**.
  **Refresh all displays**, **Check for updates** and the install picker left
  the Device Manager (checks run on connect and hourly). The split prepares the
  0.5 frontend redesign, which overhauls the Device Manager.
- **Titles fit their header** — panel titles and the built-in popup titles are
  single words where possible (**Unlock**, **Update**), and every title is
  measured with the display font and fitted to its header widget: a longer
  one ends in `..`.
- **Notifications without an icon show none** — a notification sent without
  an icon showed its severity's default icon (`mdi:information-outline`,
  `mdi:alert-outline`, `mdi:alert-octagon-outline`). It now shows no icon, and
  the message fills the full-width text box (the full height in portrait), so
  more fits per page. The severity still colours an icon you send.
- **A hub reconnect is no interaction** — the firmware's inactivity timer is a
  single rollover-safe millisecond clock that only touches and (with
  `use_button_interaction`) button presses reset. A reconnect, for example
  after a Home Assistant restart, no longer lights a dark display for another
  dimming timeout, and changing a brightness or timeout setting no longer
  counts as activity either. The hub restarts the idle-page timeout after the
  restored page is displayed, so it opens `timeout_page` seconds after the
  reconnect. A tap on a widget counts even when it is shorter than the 200 ms
  touch poll. The change ships in the firmware.
- **The idle page and auto-navigate-home run from one hub check** — the hub
  re-reads the activity clock, the active Day/Night profile and the page's hold
  once a second, so a popup that holds the idle page off, a reconnect, a saved
  timeout or a missed firmware event cannot leave the timer stopped. A changed
  `timeout_page` applies on the next check instead of after the next page
  change, and the idle page and auto-navigate-home no longer keep separate
  one-shot timers that could disagree.

### Development tooling

- **Scripts run as modules from the repository root** — the development tools
  moved into subject-named folders (`scripts/hmi_layout`, `scripts/font_tools`,
  `scripts/backgrounds`, `scripts/preview_gallery`, `scripts/translations`, …)
  and run as `python -m scripts.<folder>.<script>` from the repository root,
  without installing the repository or setting `PYTHONPATH`; the git hooks,
  the workflows and the docs use the same form. `scripts/README.md` describes
  every tool and the outputs it writes.

## Fixed

### Display and theme

- **Hub disconnects no longer leave the panel bright or dark forever** — the
  firmware immediately shows the System page and raises brightness for the
  configured dimming timeout (`timeout_dim`, including its ramp). After that,
  it dims if auto-dimming is enabled; it stays awake and never automatically
  powers the display off while disconnected. When HAUI reconnects, the hub
  restores the current panel and the firmware provides the same full-brightness
  grace before normal interaction-age dim/off behavior resumes. Reconnect does
  not reset the inactivity timer. The hub's `hub_connection_closed` action is
  authoritative even if another ESPHome API client remains connected, so the
  device-disabled-in-another-HA-instance case still gets the disconnect
  behavior. See [Device](docs/device.md#display-state-dimmed-off-and-on) and
  [ESPHome](docs/esphome.md#connection-scripts).
- **Cycle cards are no longer clipped** — the clock's date card ("Mon 16"), a
  12-hour time with AM/PM and wide temperatures ran past the big time widget.
  Each card is now measured with the display font and switches to a shorter
  form that fits: the day number with the full date below it, the time without
  AM/PM, `21°` instead of `21°C`; entity values round before dropping their
  unit. A font without a glyph for one of the characters is skipped: the
  largest fonts hold Latin-1 only, so a Polish `zamknięta` is drawn smaller
  instead of with a gap.
- **Panels follow the `background` colour override** — the hub cleared the
  page with the overridden `background`, but the HMI draws every flat widget
  (texts, icons, flat buttons) in its own page colour, so on the row,
  settings, notification, climate, timer, cover, light, media, vacuum, QR and
  alarm/unlock pages those widgets stayed dark grey boxes on the themed page.
  The hub now gives them the theme's `background` too; which widgets the HMI
  compiles with a theme colour is exported to
  `haui/mapping/theme_widgets.json`. Legacy alarm keypad colour values now
  default to the scheme's `background` and `component_text` instead of the
  fixed default palette.
- **Controls follow `component_background`** — slider tracks and the media
  progress bar kept the HMI's fixed grey, so the **Component → Background**
  colour did nothing on content pages. They now use it. With the default theme
  these tracks are one step darker than before ([40, 40, 40] instead of
  [49, 49, 49]), matching the documented page < header < cards < pressed steps.
- **Pressed buttons follow `component_pressed`** — the header buttons, flat
  buttons (timer arrows, alarm keys, media and cover controls, select and row
  buttons) and the highlighted climate mode and light function tiles kept the
  HMI's compiled pressed grey, so overriding **Component → Pressed** changed
  almost nothing. Their pressed state now uses it. The climate setpoint arrows
  and the vacuum entity buttons, which pressed to a lighter grey
  ([115, 115, 115]) left over from before the dark theme, press like every
  other button now.
- **Pages load in the device's colours** — the hub repainted a page in the
  theme colours after the display had already shown it in its compiled ones,
  so with colour overrides every page switch showed the default colours
  first. Now the hub sends
  the theme colours right before each page switch and the page paints itself
  with them while it loads (its `Preinitialize` code in the new display TFT),
  so nothing changes colour once a page is visible. Saving new colours reloads
  the page on screen, so they show at once. Until the **HAUI Display** update
  installs the new TFT, solid pages keep their compiled colours.
- **Saved panel options apply at once** — a new background of the clock, word
  clock or weather panel on screen, and the word clock's options, took effect
  only on the next page change; saving now reloads the page when it needs to.
- **Temperature text stays grey** — the clock and weather temperature text
  turned from grey to white a moment after the page appeared. It now follows
  the scheme's `text` colour, as do the clock, word clock and weather
  time/date text and cycle cards, so a light background stays readable (new
  display TFT).
- **QR and Settings pages follow the scheme** — the QR page's SSID/password
  labels and values used the HMI's compiled dark-theme colours, and so did the
  Settings brightness labels, percentages and icons. They now use the scheme's
  `text`, `text_inactive` and `component_active` colours and stay legible with
  a light scheme.
- **The Light panel title falls back** — a light entity without a name left
  the panel title empty; the configured panel title is used now, like on the
  other single-entity panels.
- **Light power button no longer turns black** — an on/off or brightness-only
  light reports no `rgb_color`, so its centre power button was drawn black
  (invisible on the dark theme) while the light was on. It now uses the
  `entity_on` colour.
- **Quotes and backslashes in display text** — text was sent to the display
  without escaping, so a `"` in a notification, title or entity name ended the
  command's string early and the text (or the whole command) was lost, and a
  trailing `\` swallowed the closing quote. Both are now escaped as the Nextion
  expects (`\"`, `\\`); a `\r` written into a configured text still forces a
  line break. The editor's live preview decodes the same escapes.
- **Stale time after waking the display** — clock, word clock, weather and
  alarm pages keep updating while the display is off (the Nextion stays awake
  at brightness 0 with the hub connected), so a wake touch shows the current
  time and states instead of those from when the display turned off.

### Hardware

- **The relays keep their last state across reboots** — `relay_left` and
  `relay_right` used `ALWAYS_OFF`, so every firmware update, reboot and power
  loss switched connected loads off. They use `RESTORE_DEFAULT_OFF` now: the
  last state is stored in the ESP32's NVS and restored on boot
  ([ESPHome](docs/esphome.md#interaction)).

### Navigation and popups

- **Stacked panels and popups show the up arrow** — a cover, light, climate,
  media, vacuum, timer or alarm panel outside navigation was treated as a popup
  because its page *can* pop up, and a popup's header showed home where the up
  arrow belongs (and no second button). Every panel opened on top of another —
  stacked panel or popup (`popup_*`) — now shows the up arrow first and home
  second (with the home button enabled), with close on the right.
- **Stacked grids and rows keep their close button** — with more than one page,
  a grid or row panel outside navigation put its next-page button on the
  right-hand slot, where close belongs, so the header had no close button.
  Pagination now always sits on the inner right slot beside the title, as it
  does in navigation.
- **Grid, row and clock tiles navigate and run actions again** — the
  availability check that hides the controls of an `unknown` or `unavailable`
  entity also covered internal items, which have no entity state at all, so a
  tile configured with `navigate:` or `action:` opened the entity-unavailable
  notification instead of switching the page or running the action. Internal
  items are always executable now; only entity-backed items are gated by their
  state.
- **The unlock popup shows its keypad and title again** — the alarm page hides
  its keypad when it loads and the alarm panel shows it again, but the unlock
  popup on the same page did not, so a PIN-protected panel opened onto an
  empty screen with no way to enter the PIN. Its title also stayed empty when
  the locked panel has none: the system panel's empty title replaced the
  fallback, now **Unlock** (was **Unlock Panel**). The popup has the header of
  the panel it locks: previous, home and next for a navigation panel, up, home
  and close for a stacked one, with the lock on the right; guarding a
  navigation panel with the home button on, it showed home in place of
  previous. Those buttons and swiping work every time now: the popup kept the
  guarded panel's navigation state after it closed, so from its second opening
  on navigation took the popup itself for the current panel and previous/next
  did nothing. Closing the popup of a locked navigation panel (the
  `close_panel` service) goes to the home panel: returning to the still-locked
  panel only opened the popup again.
- **Popups no longer leave the display's automatic behaviours off** — a popup
  holds the automatic page switch (and, unless it is a queued notification,
  **Use Auto-Dimming** and **Use Auto Display-Off**) off while it is shown; the
  settings panel does so for auto-dimming, the big QR code for auto-dimming and
  automatic page switching. The page hold lives in the hub now, not in a
  firmware switch. The firmware switches are read back by the hub, and Home
  Assistant reports a switch the hub just turned on only once the device
  confirmed it, so a popup that a saved config reopened right away found the
  switches "off" and never turned them on again: the display stopped dimming
  until the next reconnect. Popups no longer switch anything themselves: they
  only say which behaviours they hold off, and the hub sets each switch to its
  setting (Day/Night profile and sleep schedule included), or off while the
  popup on screen holds it, on every page change.
- **Automation feedback on display switches is bounded and visible** — the hub
  still restores its effective values when an auto-dimming or auto-display-off
  switch changes, but it records its own pending writes so they are not treated
  as external changes. If another automation or HA instance repeatedly changes
  the same switch, HAUI logs the likely feedback-loop causes and, after three
  rapid overrides, pauses corrections for that switch until the next device
  connect or settings save. This prevents an endless on/off loop while making
  the conflict diagnosable. These switches are hub-owned outputs: use the HAUI
  Sleep schedule or Day/Night Profiles rather than automations to drive them.
  See [Device Configuration](docs/configuration/device.md#display-dimming-off).
- **The display no longer turns off with auto display-off disabled** — the
  hub set the firmware's auto switches only on start, reconnect and a settings
  save, and only when Home Assistant reported them available. A switch turned
  on anywhere else, or restored by the device, stayed on until then. Earlier
  firmware hid that: every reconnect, and the hub used to lose the connection
  whenever it was busy, also reset the interaction timer, so the display
  rarely reached the display-off timeout. With the honest interaction timer
  and the stable connection of this release, the display turned off after
  `timeout_display_off`. The hub now follows the switches' state and sets one
  back to its setting as soon as it reports a change, except that repeated
  external overrides pause correction as described above.
- **The display turns off even with auto-dimming disabled** — the firmware's
  brightness script returned early when **Use Auto-Dimming** was off, before it
  checked the display-off timeout, so the display never reached brightness 0
  with dimming off. Brightness and display state now come from one
  `update_display` script that evaluates both switches from the same
  interaction age, and the state event is published only when it actually
  changes.

### Clock, weather and values

- **Internal temperature on clock/weather panels** — the registry lookup now
  works in production (Home Assistant's `HomeAssistant` object has no
  `helpers` attribute; the hub uses `homeassistant.helpers.entity_registry`),
  and the home temperature stays visible when the weather entity has no
  temperature attribute.
- **Clock and weather panels show 0 °C** — an outside temperature of exactly
  0 °C was treated as missing, so the temperature (and on the weather panel
  the pressure) disappeared at freezing point. A weather entity shown as a
  row or info value had the same problem.
- **Clock temperature card on opening** — a clock whose first card is the
  outside or inside temperature drew it before reading the panel's weather
  entity: `--°C` on the first open, the previous panel's weather afterwards.
- **Whole numbers without ".0"** — the weather pressure, the climate current
  temperature and a weather entity's row value print `1012hPa` / `21°C`
  instead of `1012.0hPa` / `21.0°C`, so the panel and the editor preview
  show the same text.

### Notifications

- **An open notification is no longer replaced by the next one** — the hub
  recognised its notification popup and list by the panel type
  (`popup_notify`), but those panels have the page's type (`notify`,
  `select`), so the check never matched on a device: a force-show
  notification opened over the one being read, and the open list did not
  refresh when a notification arrived. The check now uses the panel key.
- **Notification paging keeps the dismiss button** — the manual next-page
  button moved from the left-secondary to the inner-right header slot, so the
  outer-right **Dismiss** button stays available on buttonless notification
  popups (update notices, entity-unavailable, timer).
- **Notification popups no longer keep the display lit** — a queued
  notification popup suspended auto-dimming and auto display-off until it was
  dismissed, so a notification at night switched a dark panel on at full
  brightness and left it on. It now only holds off the automatic page switch;
  the display dims and turns off on its normal timers. A force-shown
  notification and a persistent alert's re-opened popup wake the display
  explicitly, except during quiet hours.
- **Persistent alert sound and quiet hours** — a persistent notification that
  arrived during quiet hours never started its repeating sound, not even after
  quiet hours ended, and one that arrived before them kept sounding through
  them. The repeat now always runs and is silent inside quiet hours.
- **Notification indicator blink runs on the hub's worker** — the blink timer
  ran page code on a thread of its own, racing page switches; it now uses the
  app's timers and skips blink ticks while the display is off.
- **Notification text fits the popup** — paging counted characters with
  guessed per-line figures, so short lines (e.g. the "Entity unavailable"
  text) overflowed the text box while ordinary messages were split across
  pages they did not need ("Someone is at the front door" took two pages at
  the large font). Text is now wrapped with the display fonts' real glyph
  widths (exported from the HMI to `haui/mapping/font_metrics.json`), a page
  holds the lines the box is tall and no more than the widget stores, and the
  automatic text size picks the largest font that fits the whole message on
  one page.
- **Notification ids are unique** — the `id` in `nspanel_haui.notification`
  events and the editor inbox was a Python object id, which is reused as soon
  as a notification is freed, so automations could mix notifications up and a
  stale inbox could dismiss the wrong one.
- **Notification line breaks** — multi-line notification text renders its
  line breaks on the display instead of breaking the display command.

### Updates and releases

- **Dev releases are tagged with their version** — a `dev` prerelease is now
  tagged with its PEP 440 version (for example `0.4.5.dev123`) instead of
  `dev-<run>-<sha>`, and the tag points at a release commit that carries that
  same version in the integration `manifest.json`. The Marketplace (like HACS
  before it) reads release tags as available versions; the old unparseable tags
  compared by plain string inequality, so an installed dev build kept offering
  itself as an update and dev releases were listed without a usable order. Dev
  releases now compare (and sort) correctly; already installed `dev-*` builds
  are offered the next versioned dev release once. The version carries no
  `+g<sha>` build segment (the commit is in the release name): AwesomeVersion
  sorts such a build above its final release and above later plain dev builds,
  so it would never be offered either. Dev builds published with the segment
  before 2026-11-04 need one manual install of a newer build. Only the newest
  10 dev prereleases are kept, so the latest stable release stays within the
  30 releases the Marketplace reads.
- **Firmware update notice compared the display TFT by mistake** — the
  "Update available" popup on the panel compared the newest GitHub release
  with the installed display `tft_version` instead of the installed firmware
  `yaml_version` (they can differ on firmware-only releases). It now compares
  like for like, so an up-to-date display can no longer hide a firmware update
  (nor a stale display invent one), and the version line shows
  `yaml_version → release`.
- **The release notice opens once per release** — a check that found the same
  release again opened another notice. The hub remembers the release it showed
  (in memory, so the notice can appear again after a restart or a channel
  change), so repeated checks no longer interrupt the panel.
- **TFT updates no longer infer the required version from the firmware** — a
  firmware that did not report `tft_required_version` was treated as requiring
  its own `yaml_version`, so a display could be flagged outdated (or updated)
  on a guess. The hub now checks the TFT only when the firmware reports
  `tft_required_version`; the Device Manager shows **Unknown** instead of
  inventing a version.
- **An install without a reboot is a failure** — a TFT upload or firmware
  install ends with the panel rebooting. A panel that reconnected without
  rebooting (its uptime is longer than the install took) was reported as
  updated; it is now reported as failed, with the reason in the Device Manager
  and on the update entity (see
  [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md#tft-install-fails-with-the-panel-did-not-reboot-after-the-upload)).
- **A failed TFT upload can be retried** — after a failed upload, a second
  attempt in the same boot stopped after 4 KB with `Invalid range end`, so the
  panel had to be restarted first. The vendored `nextion` component now resets
  its upload state at the start of every upload.
- **Custom builds find their TFT** — a custom firmware build whose update
  channel's manifest ships no TFT for it now installs the TFT from the GitHub
  release of its own firmware version.
- **Updates never stall the panel** — release checks, manifest reads and
  install downloads ran on the panel's worker thread in the hub, so a slow
  GitHub answer froze touches and page changes and could delay the hub's
  heartbeat until the panel dropped the connection and woke its display. The
  network work now runs off the worker, and the heartbeat runs on Home
  Assistant's event loop, independent of anything the panel's worker does.
- **A malformed install request installs nothing** — an install request to
  the editor's API with an unreadable body was taken as "install the offered
  firmware on every panel"; it is refused now.

### Integration

- **Cleared number fields use the default** — the panel editor saved an emptied
  number field as `0`, so clearing **Seconds per card** cycled every second and
  clearing the alarm's **Keypad font** picked the smallest font. An empty field
  now unsets the option and the panel uses its default.
- **Services accept the device their selector offers** — the services' device
  selector offers a panel's **NSPanel HAUI** device, but the services only
  matched its ESPHome device, so a device picked in the UI did nothing. Both
  devices of a panel are accepted now (and a device that is no panel fails,
  see Before updating).
- **Device Manager and Device Info details** — the TFT picker names the TFT
  version the firmware requires (its `tft_required_version`), not the firmware
  version; **Download firmware** opens the latest stable release and skips dev
  prereleases; a disabled panel's menu offers only **Enable**, reordering,
  **Settings** and **Remove**, not actions that need a running panel; a
  reorder that fails keeps the old order; **Remove** asks for confirmation
  before it deletes the panel's settings and panels.
- **ESPHome entity ids resolve through the entity registry again** —
  `HAAdapter.find_entity_id` used `hass.helpers.entity_registry`, which no
  longer exists in Home Assistant, so it always returned nothing and the config
  sync fell back to `switch.<device>_*`. With area-prefixed entity ids that id
  does not exist, and Home Assistant logged the referenced entities as missing.
  The lookup now uses `homeassistant.helpers.entity_registry`
  ([#77](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/pull/77)).
- **System Health no longer crashes** — opening the System Health page raised
  `TypeError: 'Integration' object can't be awaited`. Linking and unloading a
  panel also no longer pass the deprecated `add_config_entry_id` /
  `remove_config_entry_id` device registry arguments (they break in Home
  Assistant 2027.8): the ESPHome integration owns the device, and the hub only
  merges its `nspanel_haui` identifier
  ([#77](https://github.com/happydasch/nspanel_haui/pull/77)).

## Known limits

- The live preview and panel cards render fonts with Home Assistant's Roboto
  sized to the Nextion's, so text can sit a pixel or two differently from the
  panel.
- An install **From local file** needs Home Assistant's **Internal URL** to be
  set and reachable from the panel: the panel downloads the file from there.
